<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The move command, its answer, and the gripper calibration. [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/06-operation/how-it-works/)
explains what the gripper does with them.

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA, the grip force; not clamped by the firmware, keep it at or below the stepper's rated current (Force and speed) |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 idle |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | 1 going to the position, 0 idle, auto-release or calibrating |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Node ID, stopping, saving, resetting, clearing errors, the watchdog and the heartbeat setup: the driver's system
messages a gripper host uses.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). Setting the ID also sets the bootloader's board ID. The driver answers to the new ID at once; the ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 15 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog: every valid CAN frame the driver receives resets it; when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and stops. 0 turns it off (the default). The action byte is stored but not acted on by this firmware: the driver always stops into its idle behaviour.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 |  | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 idle, 1 hold, 2 brake (stored only) |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/ -->

# Status requests

Remote frames the host sends under a command ID, answered by the gripper with a data frame under the same ID,
and the heartbeat the gripper sends on its own when it is set up.

### Send_Respond_Ping

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 10</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Ping()`</span></div>

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Ping**.

---

### Send_Respond_Temperature

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 23</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Temperature()`</span></div>

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Temperature**.

---

### Send_Respond_Voltage

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 24</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Voltage()`</span></div>

Asks for the supply voltage.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | voltage | unsigned 16-bit | mV |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Voltage**.

---

### Send_Respond_Device_Info

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 25</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Device_Info()`</span></div>

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

**The frame** (7 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | HARDWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision |
| 1 |  | BATCH_DATE | unsigned 8-bit | production batch |
| 2 |  | SOFTWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | firmware release, e.g. 108 |
| 3-6 |  | SERIAL_NUMBER | unsigned 32-bit | serial number |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Device_Info**.

---

### Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 26</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()`</span></div>

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated and watchdog states.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | error | bit | any error is active |
| 0 | 6 | temperature_error | bit | motor over the temperature limit |
| 0 | 5 | encoder_error | bit | magnet not detected or misaligned |
| 0 | 4 | vbus_error | bit | supply voltage outside the limits |
| 0 | 3 | driver_error | bit | the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent |
| 0 | 2 | velocity_error | bit | speed over the limit |
| 0 | 1 | current_error | bit | reserved; never set by this firmware |
| 0 | 0 | estop_error | bit | Send_ESTOP was received |
| 1 | 7 | calibrated | bit | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | 6 | activated | bit | the controller is activated |
| 1 | 5 | watchdog_error | bit | the watchdog ran out |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors**.

---

### Respond_Heartbeat

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 9</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

The commands a gripper needs over the driver's serial port, for the firmware release this site describes. The
kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the
descriptions are written by hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/06-operation/uart/) says where the port is and how it is
used.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored.
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the number at most 19; the line ends with LF (CR before it is
  fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the parser does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## The commands a gripper needs

| Command | Kind | Argument | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`#Cal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Calibrated`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#CANID`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Cbw`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#Clear`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Default`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Error`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Gripact`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Action |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcur`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripinfo`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Get |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripper`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Grippos`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripstop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripvel`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Help`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Ilim`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Info`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Kiiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#Kpiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#Kt`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#L`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#LED`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Magnet`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Mode`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#PP`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#R`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | float | Driver setup |
| [`#Reset`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Save`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Temp`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |

The driver's other commands (motion, gains, the calibration settings) are in the
[STEPFOC UART reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/reference/uart/).

## By group

- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode, the gripper calibration, the setpoints, the state
- [Driver setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/): the defaults, the motor parameters and calibration, the gains, the thermistor, the node ID, saving
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/): identity, errors, temperature, help

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Gripper` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether this driver is a gripper. A gripper has it set and saved; `#Default` clears it, so set it again after restoring the defaults. | the flag |
| `#Gripcal` | Action |  | Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Enters **gripper calibration** mode. | `Gripper calibration!` |
| `#Gripinfo` | Get |  | Prints the gripper state: calibrated, activated, end stops, position, current. | the report |
| `#Gripstop` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The gripper E-stop bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripact` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The activate bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripcur` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current limit of gripper moves, the grip force. The firmware does not clamp it; keep it at or below the stepper's rated current (see Force and speed). | the setpoint |
| `#Gripvel` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 255 | The speed setpoint of gripper moves. | the setpoint |
| `#Grippos` | Set/Get | int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed) | The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode. Enters **gripper** mode. | the current position |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/setup/ -->

# Driver setup

The driver commands a self-built gripper is configured with; [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/build/first-run/)
is the procedure.

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Kpiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Kp of the Iq current loop; also sets Kpid. | the current value |
| `#Kiiq` | Set/Get | float: gain | Ki of the Iq current loop; also sets Kiid. | the current value |
| `#R` | Set/Get | float: resistance in Ω | The phase resistance of the motor (one coil). STEPFOC does not measure it; enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#L` | Set/Get | float: inductance in H | The phase inductance of the motor (one coil); enter the datasheet value before Cal. | the current value |
| `#Kt` | Set/Get | float: Nm/A | The torque constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Cal` | Action |  | Runs the driver's motor calibration (see Driver configuration): enter PP, R and L first, with the pinion not yet in the rack. | the calibration log |
| `#Save` | Action |  | Writes the configuration to the EEPROM. Do it after calibration and after tuning. | `Save` |
| `#Ilim` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The driver's Iq current limit outside gripper mode; the firmware clamps it to 2800 mA. Gripper moves use Gripcur instead. | the current limit |
| `#Tlim` | Set/Get | int: temperature in °C | The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. | `Temp limit N` |
| `#Default` | Action |  | Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM, including the serial number, hardware version and batch date, and clears the gripper flag, heartbeat and watchdog. Back those up first. | `Loaded default config!` |
| `#Term` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). | the setting |
| `#Cbw` | Set/Get | float: bandwidth in Hz | The current loop bandwidth calibration uses to compute Kpiq and Kiiq. | the bandwidth |
| `#CANID` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 13 | The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Setting the ID also sets the bootloader's board ID. Kept over a power cycle after Save. | the ID, or `Invalid CAN ID` |
| `#PP` | Set/Get | int: pole pairs | The motor's pole pairs: 50 for a 1.8° stepper, 75 for 1.2°, 100 for 0.9°, 125 for 0.72°. Calibration accepts only these values. | the current value |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/uart/utility/ -->

# Status and utility

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Magnet` | Get |  | Reads the encoder's magnet status. | `Magnet Good` or `Magnet Bad` |
| `#Reset` | Action |  | Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. | nothing |
| `#Temp` | Get |  | Prints the thermistor temperature. | °C, or `Temp Off` while the thermistor is disabled |
| `#Mode` | Get |  | Prints the control mode. | `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`, `Open loop`, `Gripper mode` |
| `#Vbus` | Get |  | Prints the supply voltage. | mV |
| `#Error` | Get |  | Prints which errors are active. | `No errors!` or `In error state!` followed by one line per active error |
| `#Clear` | Action |  | Clears the errors and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or `#Calibrated 1`). Enters **idle** mode. | `Clear errors` |
| `#Help` | Action |  | Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 108. | the reference |
| `#Info` | Get |  | Prints the driver's identity and state: hardware and firmware version, serial number, motor parameters, calibration, errors. | the report |
| `#Calibrated` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The calibrated flag. `#Calibrated 1` clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. | the flag |
| `#LED` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Turns the status LED on or off. | the LED state |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/errors/ -->

# Errors and status bits

## The gripper's state byte

Byte 3 of Respond_Gripper_data_pack, the answer to every gripper command, bits numbered from the most significant:

| Bit | Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `activated` | the activate flag is set |
| 6 | `action_status` | 1 while a move is in progress; 0 when idle, holding, auto-releasing or calibrating |
| 5, 4 | `object_detection` | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object found while closing, 2 object found while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | `temperature_error` | the thermistor on the motor housing is above the limit |
| 2 | `timeout_error` | the driver's CAN watchdog ran out |
| 1 | `estop_error` | the E-stop bit of a command was received |
| 0 | `calibrated` | the gripper calibration is done |

The Python library's attributes are `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`,
`gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error` and `gripper_calibrated`; library
version 1.20 assembles `gripper_object_detection` with its two bits swapped (1 and 2 exchanged).

## The driver's error flags

The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line `#Error` prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of
Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

| Flag | `#Error` prints | Byte, bit | Raised when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Error` | `In error state!` | 0, 7 | any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) |
| `temperature_error` | `Temp error` | 0, 6 | the thermistor reads above `#Tlim` (75 °C) |
| `encoder_error` | `Encoder error` | 0, 5 | the driver's encoder does not see its magnet |
| `Vbus_error` | `Vbus error` | 0, 4 | the supply is below 9 V or above 29.5 V |
| `Driver_error` | `Driver error (undervoltage, thermal shutdown, or overcurrent)` | 0, 3 | the driver stage's fault output is active |
| `Velocity_error` | `Velocity error` | 0, 2 | the motor speed exceeds the driver's limit |
| `Current_error` | `Current error` | 0, 1 | never in this firmware; reserved |
| `ESTOP_error` | `Received ESTOP command` | 0, 0 | Send_ESTOP was received |
| `Calibrated` (0) | `Not calibrated` | 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) | the driver's motor calibration is missing |
| `Activated` | — | 1, 6 | the activated flag, not an error |
| `Watchdog_error` | `Watchdog error` | 1, 5 | the watchdog time passed without a valid CAN frame |

The gripper's `timeout_error` is the driver's `Watchdog_error`; the gripper's `temperature_error` is the driver's.
The gripper's `estop_error` is its own, raised by the E-stop bit of the gripper command, and is distinct from the
driver's `ESTOP_error` raised by Send_ESTOP.

## Clearing

Send_Clear_Error and `#Clear` clear every flag, the gripper's E-stop included, and go to idle; a flag whose cause
persists is set again at once. After an E-stop, the next gripper command must carry the E-stop bit at 0. The
driver's `Calibrated` flag is set only by the motor calibration (`#Cal`).

## The LED

The driver's status LED is inside the housing: three short flashes and a pause in normal operation, flashing
every 0.5 s during the motor calibration, on steadily in error mode or while the motor is not calibrated.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/python/ -->

# Python library

The `Spectral-BLDC` package ([Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python),
`pip install Spectral-BLDC`) has one method per CAN message in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, and
`Spectral_BLDC.CanCommunication` for the bus. [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/06-operation/python/) shows how they are used
with the gripper.

## Calls and messages

The calls for the messages this reference describes; the library has one for every message of the driver.

| Library call | Sends | Answered with | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Send_gripper_data_pack()` | Send_gripper_data_pack (ID 61) | Respond_Gripper_data_pack | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) |
| `Send_gripper_calibrate()` | Send_gripper_calibrate (ID 62) | — | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) |
| `Send_CAN_ID()` | Send_CAN_ID (ID 11) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_can_id) |
| `Send_ESTOP()` | Send_ESTOP (ID 0) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_estop) |
| `Send_Idle()` | Send_Idle (ID 12) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_idle) |
| `Send_Save_config()` | Send_Save_config (ID 13) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) |
| `Send_Reset()` | Send_Reset (ID 14) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_reset) |
| `Send_Clear_Error()` | Send_Clear_Error (ID 1) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) |
| `Send_Watchdog()` | Send_Watchdog (ID 15) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) |
| `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()` | Send_Heartbeat_Setup (ID 30) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) |
| `Send_Respond_Ping()` | Send_Respond_Ping (ID 10) | Send_Respond_Ping (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/#send_respond_ping) |
| `Send_Respond_Temperature()` | Send_Respond_Temperature (ID 23) | Send_Respond_Temperature (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) |
| `Send_Respond_Voltage()` | Send_Respond_Voltage (ID 24) | Send_Respond_Voltage (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/#send_respond_voltage) |
| `Send_Respond_Device_Info()` | Send_Respond_Device_Info (ID 25) | Send_Respond_Device_Info (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/#send_respond_device_info) |
| `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()` | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (ID 26) | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors) |

`Send_gripper_data_pack(position, speed, current, activate, action, estop, release_direction)` sends the 5-byte
move; called without arguments it sends the empty frame that only asks for the state.

## Receiving

`CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout)` returns `(message, ids)`: the raw `python-can` message and a tuple
`ids` with `node_id`, `command_id` and `error_bit` from the identifier, or `(None, None)` after the timeout.
`SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids)` decodes the message into the object's attributes:

| Message | Attributes |
|---|---|
| Respond_Gripper_data_pack | `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated` |
| Send_Respond_State_of_Errors | `error`, `temperature_error`, `encoder_error`, `vbus_error`, `driver_error`, `velocity_error`, `current_error`, `estop_error`, `calibrated`, `activated`, `watchdog_error` |
| Send_Respond_Temperature | `temperature` |
| Send_Respond_Voltage | `voltage` |
| Send_Respond_Device_Info | `HARDWARE_VERSION`, `BATCH_DATE`, `SOFTWARE_VERSION`, `SERIAL_NUMBER` |

!!! note "Object detection in the library"
    Library version 1.20 assembles `gripper_object_detection` with the two bits swapped relative to the firmware,
    so it reports 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1 (object
    detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. Until the library is fixed, swap the two values in your
    program, or read the bits yourself from the frame.

# Guides

Worked examples around the gripper.

- [Basic control in Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/guides/basic-control/): the shortest program that calibrates the gripper and opens and
  closes it, from the product repository's README.
- [Teleoperation with two grippers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/guides/teleoperation/): one gripper follows the other and pushes back what it
  feels, over one CAN bus and a few lines of Python.

Building a gripper yourself is in the manual, the [Build guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/build/). More examples,
for the driver as much as for the gripper, are in the
[Spectral-BLDC-Python examples](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples) and in
the [STEPFOC guides](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/guides/).

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/guides/basic-control/ -->

# Basic control in Python

The shortest program that drives the gripper: it connects through the CANvas adapter, clears the errors,
calibrates, then closes and opens every three seconds and prints what the gripper answers. It is the example from
the product repository's README; `pip install Spectral-BLDC` is the only requirement. Change `COM20` to your
adapter's port (`/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux) and `node_id` to the gripper's CAN ID if you changed it from 0.

!!! danger
    700 mA closes the jaws with real force, about 14 N with the 21.5 mm stepper and 25 N with the 60 mm. Keep fingers out of the jaws, and start with a lower current
    if the gripper is new to you.

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import time

Communication1 = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM20', bitrate=1000000)
Motor1 = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=Communication1)

Motor1.Send_Clear_Error()
Motor1.Send_gripper_calibrate()
time.sleep(4)

temp_var = 0
while True:
   if temp_var == 0:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(50,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 1
   elif temp_var == 1:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(240,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 0

   message, UnpackedMessageID = Communication1.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.2)

   if message is not None:
      print(f"Message is: {message}")
      print(f"Node ID is : {UnpackedMessageID.node_id}")
      print(f"Message ID is: {UnpackedMessageID.command_id}")
      print(f"Error bit is: {UnpackedMessageID.error_bit}")
      print(f"Timestamp is: {message.timestamp}")

   time.sleep(3)
```

The arguments of `Send_gripper_data_pack`, in order: the position (0 open, 255 closed), the speed (0 to 255), the
current limit in mA (the force), then the activate bit, the action bit, the E-stop bit and the release direction.
[With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/06-operation/python/) explains the library's calls, [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/06-operation/how-it-works/)
the state the gripper answers with, and [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) what the
current means in newtons.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/guides/teleoperation/ -->

# Teleoperation with two grippers

Two grippers on one CAN bus, coupled so that each follows the other: squeeze one by hand and the other closes;
when the other meets an object, the one in your hand pushes back with the force it feels. A hundred lines of
Python, and the basis of a teleoperation setup with force feedback.

This guide does not use the gripper mode. Both drivers run in **current (torque) mode**, the driver's own motion
command, and the PC closes a position loop between them at a fixed rate. The gripper mode's position, speed and
object detection are not involved; the drivers are plain torque sources here.

## What you need

- Two grippers, calibrated as motors (a bought gripper is), with different node IDs: 0 and 1 (`#CANID 1`,
  `#Save` on one of them over UART).
- Both on one bus with the CANvas adapter, 24 V on both, termination at the two ends.
- `pip install Spectral-BLDC SourceRoboticsToolbox`.

!!! warning
    In current mode the gripper has no end-stop knowledge and no object detection: it pushes with whatever current
    the loop commands. Set the driver's current limit to the stepper's rating (`#Ilim`) on both grippers, start
    with low gains, and keep fingers out of the jaws.

## The idea

Each driver is commanded a current proportional to the difference between the two positions, plus a damping
term on the speed difference and a little damping of its own motion:

$$
I_0 = K_p\,(p_1 - p_0) + K_d\,(v_1 - v_0) - K_k\, v_0, \qquad
I_1 = K_p\,(p_0 - p_1) + K_d\,(v_0 - v_1) - K_k\, v_1
$$

$p$ is the jaw position of each gripper in the same units, $v$ its speed. When the two positions agree, both
currents are zero and the grippers rest. Move one by hand and the difference drives the other after it; block
the other, and the difference drives the one in your hand back with the same current, which is the force you
feel. $K_p$ is the stiffness of the virtual spring between them, $K_d$ its damping.

The two drivers' encoders do not read the same number at the same jaw position, so each position is referred to
a reference reading taken once with both grippers in the same position; the Source Robotics Toolbox's `Joint`
does that bookkeeping and unwraps the encoder over its 16384-tick turns.

## The code

```python
import time
import numpy as np
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import SourceRoboticsToolbox as Toolbox

INTERVAL_S = 0.002                 # the loop rate: 500 Hz
REFERENCE = [10440, 13555]         # each gripper's raw encoder reading with both jaws in the same position

Kp, Kd, Kk = 650, 0.0055, 0.0003   # stiffness, damping between the two, damping of each

bus = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM123', bitrate=1000000)
motors = [Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=i, communication=bus) for i in (0, 1)]
joints = [Toolbox.Joint(encoder_resolution=14, master_position=REFERENCE[i], gear_ratio=1, offset=0, dir=0)
          for i in (0, 1)]

position = np.zeros(2)             # each gripper's position, referred to its reference
sector_known = [False, False]
current = [0, 0]

while True:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for i in (0, 1):               # command the currents; each answer carries position and speed
        motors[i].Send_data_pack_1(Position=None, Speed=None, Current=int(current[i]))
    for _ in (0, 1):
        message, ids = bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.001)
        if ids is None:
            continue
        i = ids[0]
        motors[i].UnpackData(message, ids)
        if not sector_known[i]:
            joints[i].determine_sector(motors[i].position)
            sector_known[i] = True
        position[i] = joints[i].get_joint_position(motors[i].position)

    current[0] = Kp * (position[1] - position[0]) + Kd * (motors[1].speed - motors[0].speed) - Kk * motors[0].speed
    current[1] = Kp * (position[0] - position[1]) + Kd * (motors[0].speed - motors[1].speed) - Kk * motors[1].speed

    time.sleep(max(0.0, INTERVAL_S - (time.perf_counter() - t0)))
```

The reference readings: with both grippers powered and their jaws set by hand to the same opening, read each
driver's position (`#Info` over UART, or `Send_Respond_Encoder_data` from Python) and put the two numbers in
`REFERENCE`.

## Tuning

Start with `Kp` at a tenth of the value above and raise it until the follower tracks the leader without lagging;
raise `Kd` if the pair oscillates. The current the formula produces is in mA and is clamped by each driver's
`#Ilim`, so the stepper's rating is the ceiling of the force feedback. A fixed loop rate matters: a loop that
runs at an uneven rate makes the damping terms noisy.

The full example, with a timer for a precise loop rate, is
[gripper_teleop_PC_calc.py](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples/Advanced/SSG48%20gripper%20bilateral%20teleop)
in the Python library's examples, and the [bilateral teleoperation guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/STEPFOC-docs/latest/guides/bilateral-teleoperation/)
on the STEPFOC site explains the control law with a joint instead of a gripper.

# Getting help

- **Questions and discussion**: the [Source Robotics Discord](https://discord.gg/prjUvjmGpZ).
- **A problem with the gripper's hardware or its files**: an issue in the
  [product repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/MSG-compliant-AI-stepper-gripper/issues); see
  [Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/support/report-a-problem/) for what to include.
- **A problem with the firmware**: an issue in the [driver's repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/STEPFOC-stepper-controller/issues);
  with the Python library, in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/issues);
  with the ROS 2 driver, in [its repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/source_robotics_msg_gripper_ros2/issues).
- **A mistake on a page of this site**: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see
  [Contributing](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/support/contributing/).
- **Orders and hardware**: [source-robotics.com](https://source-robotics.com/).

Before you ask, [Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/09-troubleshooting/) goes through the common symptoms, and the gripper's
status tells most of what anyone will ask you for.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/support/report-a-problem/ -->

# Report a problem

Open an issue in the [product repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/MSG-compliant-AI-stepper-gripper/issues)
for the gripper and its files, in the [driver's repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/STEPFOC-stepper-controller/issues)
for the firmware, or in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/issues)
for the Python library. Include:

1. **The gripper**: bought or self-built, the rail and the stepper, the jaws.
2. **The firmware release** the gripper runs: Send_Respond_Device_Info, or `#Info` over UART, which also carries
   the driver's configuration and errors.
3. **The gripper's status** when the problem happens: the state and error bits of Respond_Gripper_data_pack, or
   `#Gripinfo`.
4. **What you did and what happened**: the commands, in order, with their position, speed and current, and the
   answers.
5. **How it is connected**: the robot or the adapter, the cable, the termination; a photo helps more than a
   description.

For a problem with this documentation, the *Report it* link at the end of the page opens an issue in the
documentation repository with the page already named.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/MSG-gripper-docs/1.1/support/contributing/ -->

# Contributing

This documentation lives in [Source-Robotics/MSG-gripper-docs](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/MSG-gripper-docs).
A small fix can be made from the browser: the *Edit it on GitHub* link at the end of every page opens the page's
source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

## How the site is built

- The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's `README.md` says how to
  preview it locally.
- The site describes one release of the STEPFOC firmware, named in `versions.yml`. The command IDs, frame
  lengths, the UART command list and what each prints in the API reference are read from the firmware's source at
  that release's tag by `tools/sync_firmware.py`; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the
  commands are in `docs/includes/can_commands.yml` and `uart_commands.yml`, which list only the commands a
  gripper needs.
- Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to `main` publishes the
  site under its firmware version with [mike](https://github.com/jimporter/mike).

## House rules

- Facts come from the firmware and the product repository. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware
  is right; fix the page, or report the firmware.
- Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
- Write for someone who has the gripper in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order,
  then why.
- Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
- Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.
